note.question: Which subscription-revenue rule protects artists' coalition incentives while aligning each listener's payment with the artists the listener actually streams?
note.overview: The paper associates each streaming-revenue problem with a convex transferable-utility cooperative game among artists and fully characterizes its core. It then uses core selection and incentive axioms to characterize the user-centric allocation rule.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: For a fixed accounting period, users generate a matrix of streams and each contributes one normalized subscription unit. The platform applies an index to allocate total revenue. Conceptually, any coalition of artists can reject the allocation and form an alternative platform whose guaranteed worth comes from users who listened exclusively to that coalition. Coalition worth uses a deliberately pessimistic secession benchmark based on exclusive listeners.
